number.why: The abstract explicitly reports HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.73–0.93) for the primary kidney composite, comparing finerenone with placebo over trial follow-up. Agreement includes the ruling's qualification: the packet establishes a full analysis set, but does not establish its equivalence to intention-to-treat.

quotes.span: The primary composite outcome, assessed in a time-to-event analysis, was kidney failure, a sustained decrease of at least 40% in the eGFR from baseline, or death from renal causes.

During a median follow-up of 2.6 years, a primary outcome event occurred in 504 of 2833 patients (17.8%) in the finerenone group and 600 of 2841 patients (21.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.93; P = 0.001).

TIME FRAME: From randomization up until the first occurrence of the primary renal composite endpoint, or censoring at the end of the study, with an average follow-up time of 32 months | POPULATION: Full analysis set

entry.why: The entry criteria establish adults with CKD and type 2 diabetes; the abstract establishes randomized, double-blind assignment to finerenone or placebo. The analysis-set uncertainty does not undermine these entry criteria.

quotes.span: Inclusion Criteria: * Men or women ≥18 years of age * Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) as defined by the American Diabetes Association * Diagnosis of chronic kidney disease (CKD)
In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 5734 patients with CKD and type 2 diabetes in a 1:1 ratio to receive finerenone or placebo.

missed: Nothing that changes either conclusion. The ruling already identifies the unsupported intention-to-treat equivalence and fulltext_verified provenance; numerical confirmation should not be interpreted as validation of those labels.
